title: Other Examples of Nested Logit Models
text: TravelMode long format: 840 rows = 210 individuals × 4 travel alternatives (air, train, bus, car). Variables wait gcost alternative-specific — differ across modes individual. nestedLogit() requires one row per individual chosen mode response. individual-specific predictors (income, size) work directly; alternative-specific costs require different approach.
code: tm <- TravelMode |>   filter(choice == "yes") |>   select(mode, income, size) |>   mutate(mode = relevel(factor(mode), ref = "car"))  table(tm$mode) #>  #>   car   air train   bus  #>    59    58    63    30

title: Other Examples of Nested Logit Models
text: canonical nested structure separates private (car) public transit, within public separates air ground, train bus. reflects IIA problem: adding near-identical alternative (e.g., second bus service) equally reduce probability choosing car.
code: travel_dichots <- logits(   pvt_pub  = dichotomy("car", public = c("air", "train", "bus")),   air_grnd = dichotomy("air", ground = c("train", "bus")),   tr_bus   = dichotomy("train", "bus") ) travel_dichots #> pvt_pub: {car} vs. public{air, train, bus} #> air_grnd: {air} vs. ground{train, bus} #> tr_bus: {train} vs. {bus}

title: Other Examples of Nested Logit Models
text: Another classic econometric dataset amenable nested dichotomies treatment concerns choice recreational anglers among different modes fishing: beach pier, boat, private charter. dataset Herriges & Kling (1999); see also Cameron & Trivedi (2005) econometric treatment. section requires mlogit package.

title: Other Examples of Nested Logit Models
text: 1182 US recreational anglers chose one four fishing modes: beach, pier, boat, charter. natural nesting separates shore-based vessel-based alternatives: Shore-based modes share unobserved attributes (boat required, lower cost commitment) vessel-based modes , IIA plausible within across groups. Unlike AER::TravelMode, mlogit::Fishing already wide format — one row per individual — mode indicating chosen alternative income individual-specific predictor. price.* catch.* variables alternative-specific (one column per mode) used directly nestedLogit(), expects predictors apply individual, alternative. full conditional-logit model (e.g., via mlogit::mlogit()) needed exploit variables.
code: fishing       /        \    shore      vessel   /     \    /      \ beach  pier boat  charter fishing_dichots <- logits(   shore_vessel = dichotomy(shore  = c("beach", "pier"),                            vessel = c("boat",  "charter")),   shore_type   = dichotomy("beach", "pier"),   vessel_type  = dichotomy("boat",  "charter") ) fishing_dichots #> shore_vessel: shore{beach, pier} vs. vessel{boat, charter} #> shore_type: {beach} vs. {pier} #> vessel_type: {boat} vs. {charter} as.tree(fishing_dichots, response = "mode") #>         mode #>       /        \ #>    shore     vessel #>    /   \      /   \ #> beach pier boat charter fish_nested <- nestedLogit(mode ~ income,                            dichotomies = fishing_dichots,                            data = Fishing) summary(fish_nested) #> Nested logit models: mode ~ income #>  #> Response shore_vessel: shore{beach, pier} vs. vessel{boat, charter} #> Call: #> glm(formula = shore_vessel ~ income, family = binomial, data = Fishing,  #>     contrasts = contrasts) #>  #> Coefficients: #>              Estimate Std. text: 84 patients double-blind clinical trial received either active treatment placebo. outcome Improved ordinal: Continuation logits natural : dichotomy 1 asks whether patient improved ; dichotomy 2 asks, given improvement, whether marked rather merely .
